name: The Entrance Bridge
facts: The Entrance Bridge first opened on 15 December 1934 as a wooden single‑lane bridge, featuring bypass bays that let traffic in the opposite direction pass, a clever solution for its era.
In 1967 construction of the current 467‑metre, 18‑span concrete girder bridge began, and it welcomed traffic on 20 December 1968, officially inaugurated by Premier Robert Askin on 18 April 1969.
The bridge carries the Central Coast Highway (A49) and a grade‑separated pedestrian footpath and cycleway, linking The Entrance with The Entrance North across the Tuggerah Lakes Entrance Channel.
